problems.q: How many moles are in 44.01 g of CO2? Use 44.01 g/mol for CO2.
problems.why: Moles = mass / molar mass = 44.01 g / 44.01 g/mol = 1.000 mol. OpenStax AF2e §6.1.
hints: Divide the gram amount by the molar mass. Do not multiply.

problems.q: You dilute 50.0 mL of 0.800 M NaCl to 200.0 mL. What is the new concentration?
problems.why: Moles of solute stay the same: M1V1 = M2V2. (0.800 M)(50.0 mL) / 200.0 mL = 0.200 M. OpenStax AF2e §6.3.
hints: The volume gets larger, so the molarity gets smaller. Keep the volume units the same on both sides.

problems.q: A sample contains 0.150 mol C, 0.450 mol H, and 0.150 mol N. What is the empirical formula? Write C, then H, then N.
problems.why: Divide each amount by 0.150 mol. The ratio is 1 mol C : 3 mol H : 1 mol N, so the empirical formula is CH3N. OpenStax AF2e §6.2.
hints: Divide all three mole counts by the smallest one, 0.150 mol.
